request: a bento box-inspired collapsible UI menu component for a fictional coffee company site
thesis: A menu that opens like a lacquered bento lid: unequal compartments of one tight grid, each holding one small thing, collapsing back to a single pill.
job: see a closed trigger/pill that says menu
pick a destination (beans, brew gear, subscribe, visit, story)
interact with a compartment state (choose roast, toggle grind or size, add to order count)
collapse it again (button, Esc, outside click)
use it by keyboard and on a phone

principles: disclosure pattern: button controls a region
tricks: Esc closes and returns focus to trigger
grid-template-rows 0fr to 1fr animates height without JS measuring

principles: one radius family, nested radii = outer minus gap
tricks: a tile with a big number or glyph reads at a glance
slightly different tile tints from one hue family
tests: squint: do sizes form a clear hierarchy

principles: lid opens, tiles settle in staggered
one state object, render from it

kinds.name: dropdown bento panel
kinds.what: pill trigger opens a grid panel below it

descriptions: voice: short, warm, a bit wry
one hero tile spans 2x2, one wide tile spans 2x1
behaviors: on narrow screens spans collapse to 2 cols

descriptions: cream page, espresso ink, caramel accent

behaviors: open: panel grows, tiles rise 8px and fade in

descriptions: roast: 3-way segmented; grind toggle; cup counter with + and -; selected label echoed in trigger or order tile

anti_keywords.instead: clear size hierarchy with a hero tile
matte warm tiles with hairline borders
every tile does something or goes somewhere
menu is not a full site: 5 to 7 tiles
system serif/sans stack, inline SVG or CSS shapes

checks: phone width has no horizontal scroll
